**Recommendation: Muskegon first, with Grand Haven a close second.** Troll glow spoons, glow plugs and meat rigs 60–100 ft down over 100–160 ft of water. The newest reports are from 2025-07-30, so they are 6 days old. I couldn't get a wind forecast or modeled cold-layer depths today, only a weekly buoy summary.

| Port | Rating | Basis |
|---|---|---|

**What the reports say**
- **Muskegon:**
  - "Salmon action was good for boat anglers" (Muskegon, 2025-07-30). The best action was 60–100 ft down in 100–160 ft of water.
  - Glow plugs, glow spoons, green rotator/fly combinations and meat rigs all worked (Muskegon, 2025-07-30).
  - The trend was slow on 07-02 and 07-09, average on 07-16 and 07-23, then good on 07-30.
- **Grand Haven:**
  - Good numbers in 100–160 ft of water, with fish 50–90 ft down (Grand Haven, 2025-07-30). Glow plugs, meat rigs and rotator/fly combinations worked best.
  - It was also rated good the week before: 60–100 ft down in 90–160 ft of water on white flasher/flies, green meat rigs and a glow spoon (Grand Haven, 2025-07-23).
- **South Haven:**
  - Productive, mostly Chinook with a few coho, in about 95 ft of water and some good results near 115 ft (South Haven, 2025-07-30). Spoons were the main bite, and meat rigs took some of the larger fish. No fish depth was given.
  - The coho were rated below average (South Haven, 2025-07-30).
  - The week before it was slow, with fish "very scattered" from 55 to over 120 ft (South Haven, 2025-07-23).
- **St. Joseph:**
  - "Decent," with fish spread from 90 to well beyond 110 ft. Rotators tipped with flies or meat rigs were most productive, and the catch was a mix of Chinook and coho (St. Joseph, 2025-07-30).
  - Earlier weeks were slow, with the warmer water noted as slowing the action (St. Joseph, 2025-07-16).

**Water:** The buoy summaries for the week before today show a sharp surface drop at every port. That is the possible-upwelling signature:
- Grand Haven and Muskegon: 67 F average, down 14 F.
- South Haven: 65 F, down 9 F.
- St. Joseph: 69 F, down 4 F.

These are measured buoy readings. Before that drop the surface was 75–77 F (reports, 2025-07-30).

**My read**
- I'd expect the cold-water shift to push fish around, and perhaps shoreward. I can't tell from the data whether that helps or hurts this week. After the 07-23 upwelling signal at Grand Haven and Muskegon, the next reports were good.
- I'd expect Muskegon and Grand Haven to stay ahead because their good ratings came two weeks in a row. South Haven is less consistent, so I rate it lower.
- St. Joseph has the warmest water and the weakest run of reports, so I'd put it last.
- I'd start at 60–100 ft down and adjust to wherever the first fish come from. Early morning and late evening were noted as productive in past Muskegon reports (2023), which is history, not this year.

**Caveats**
- I have no wind or wave forecast for this week. Check it before heading out. A June report noted weather keeping boats from deeper water (St. Joseph, 2025-06-25).
- I found no access closures in these reports.
- Similar weeks in past seasons (history) were mostly average to good at Muskegon and Grand Haven, and good at South Haven in 2024 (South Haven, 2024-07-31). That fits the ranking above.
